boundary_rationale: This row opens directly after the previous row's closing salvation promise (web:Isa.46.13) on a fresh imperative address to a new addressee: “Come down and sit in the dust, virgin daughter of Babylon. Sit on the ground without a throne, daughter of the Chaldeans. For you will no longer be called tender and delicate.” (web:Isa.47.1), רְדִ֣י וּשְׁבִ֣י (oshb:Isa.47.1, byte tier), commanding personified Babylon down from her throne. The redeemer confession “Our Redeemer, Yahweh of Armies is his name, is the Holy One of Israel.” (web:Isa.47.4) -- גֹּאֲלֵ֕נוּ יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁמ֑וֹ קְד֖וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:Isa.47.4, byte tier) -- is a brief communal aside naming the book's qadosh-Israel title rather than a fresh address to Babylon, so the row holds it as an aside inside the second-person address that brackets it: the second-feminine-singular imperatives רְדִ֣י וּשְׁבִ֣י (oshb:Isa.47.1, byte tier) that open the row and שְׁבִ֥י דוּמָ֛ם וּבֹ֥אִי (oshb:Isa.47.5, byte tier) that follow this verse both address Babylon directly, while this verse's own first-person plural confession names no addressee of its own -- a person shift, not a syntactic continuation, is the ground the aside reading rests on. The matching imperative “Sit in silence, and go into darkness, daughter of the Chaldeans. For you shall no longer be called the mistress of kingdoms.” (web:Isa.47.5) resumes the address to the same addressee named in web:Isa.47.1, continuing the same movement through Babylon's own boast, “You said, ‘I will be a princess forever,’ so that you didn’t lay these things to your heart, nor did you remember the results.” (web:Isa.47.7), the row's own closing verse before the pivot to a fresh summons formula at web:Isa.47.8.
strongest_rejected_alternative: A rival reading treats the daughter-of-Babylon address as one sustained unit through Isa.47.15, since the same addressee is argued from Isa.47.1 to Isa.47.15; this row reads the summons formula opening Isa.47.8 as a sufficient internal pivot for a cut there.
literature_type_guess: taunt-oracle pronouncing Babylon's dethronement, sealed by a communal redeemer confession

boundary_rationale: A formal pivot opens this row: “Now therefore hear this, you who are given to pleasures, who sit securely, who say in your heart, ‘I am, and there is no one else besides me.” (web:Isa.47.8), וְעַתָּ֞ה שִׁמְעִי זֹ֤את (oshb:Isa.47.8, byte tier) -- a feminine-singular hear-this collocation belonging to the same imperative-plus-cataphoric-object CLASS as the masculine-plural שִׁמְעוּ זֹ֣את (oshb:Isa.48.1, byte tier) that opens the following chapter's unit, the two disjoint under consonantal search (1 verse and 2 verses book-wide, skeleton tier, verse counts) and so a class-level tie rather than a form recurrence -- turning from the dethronement scene closing at web:Isa.47.7 to a formal announcement of disaster against the same addressee. The judgment closes on the sorcery mockery and its verdict, “Behold, they are like stubble. The fire will burn them. They won’t deliver themselves from the power of the flame. It won’t be a coal to warm at or a fire to sit by. The things that you labored in will be like this: those who have trafficked with you from your youth will each wander in his own way. There will be no one to save you.” (web:Isa.47.14-Isa.47.15), the row's own closing verses before the fresh summons formula opening the next row at web:Isa.48.1.
strongest_rejected_alternative: A rival cut would isolate the enchantments taunt opening Isa.47.12 as its own row rather than reading it as continuing the accusatory movement opened at Isa.47.8.
literature_type_guess: formal judgment-summons against Babylon's failed sorceries and astrologers

boundary_rationale: A second imperative vocative opens this row after the self-interest close of the previous row (web:Isa.48.11): “Listen to me, O Jacob, and Israel my called: I am he. I am the first. I am also the last.” (web:Isa.48.12), שְׁמַ֤ע אֵלַי֙ יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב (oshb:Isa.48.12, byte tier), a singular address distinct from the plural summons that opened the earlier row at web:Isa.48.1. The self-declaration and creation claim carry into the assembly-summons “Assemble yourselves, all of you, and hear! Who among them has declared these things? He whom Yahweh loves will do what he likes to Babylon, and his arm will be against the Chaldeans.” (web:Isa.48.14), naming Yahweh's own action against Babylon and the Chaldeans. The sender clause “Come near to me and hear this: “From the beginning I have not spoken in secret; from the time that it happened, I was there.” Now the Lord Yahweh has sent me with his Spirit.” (web:Isa.48.16) -- וְעַתָּ֗ה אֲדֹנָ֧י יְהוִ֛ה שְׁלָחַ֖נִי וְרוּחֽוֹ (oshb:Isa.48.16, byte tier) -- names a first-person speaker the row does not attribute to a decided identity; the koh-amar formula “Yahweh, your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel, says: “I am Yahweh your God, who teaches you to profit, who leads you by the way that you should go.” (web:Isa.48.17), כֹּֽה אָמַ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה (oshb:Isa.48.17, byte tier), frames the teaching that follows as Yahweh's own, and the row closes on the lament “Oh that you had listened to my commandments! Then your peace would have been like a river and your righteousness like the waves of the sea. Your offspring also would have been as the sand and the descendants of your body like its grains. His name would not be cut off nor destroyed from before me.”” (web:Isa.48.18-Isa.48.19), the row's own closing verses before the bare departure imperative opening the next row at web:Isa.48.20.
strongest_rejected_alternative: A rival cut would open a fresh row at either of two declined summons onsets. At Isa.48.16, קִרְב֧וּ אֵלַ֣י שִׁמְעוּ זֹ֗את (oshb:Isa.48.16, byte tier) -- its hear-this collocation matching שִׁמְעוּ זֹ֣את (oshb:Isa.48.1, byte tier) at accent-stripped tier, one of only 2 verses book-wide carrying that collocation at skeleton tier -- the row instead reads the sender clause that follows as completing the same predictive-proof argument opened earlier rather than starting a new movement. At Isa.48.14, הִקָּבְצ֤וּ כֻלְּכֶם֙ וּֽשֲׁמָ֔עוּ (oshb:Isa.48.14, byte tier) -- an assemble-imperative standing in 2 verses book-wide at skeleton tier (Isa.45.20 and Isa.48.14), neither site a seam elsewhere in this stretch -- the row likewise reads the verse as continuing the same self-declaration rather than opening a fresh unit.
literature_type_guess: self-declaration and Cyrus-argument trial speech opening into a teaching lament over unheeded commandments

The sender clause's first-person voice at Isa.48.16 is held open rather than assigned to a decided speaker.

boundary_rationale: A bare departure imperative opens this row: “Leave Babylon! Flee from the Chaldeans! With the sound of joyful shouting announce this, tell it even to the end of the earth; say, “Yahweh has redeemed his servant Jacob!”” (web:Isa.48.20), spliced at צְא֣וּ מִבָּבֶל֮ בִּרְח֣וּ מִכַּשְׂדִּים֒ (oshb:Isa.48.20, byte tier). The same verse also carries a causative hear-root form standing later in it, הַשְׁמִ֨יעוּ֙ זֹ֔את (oshb:Isa.48.20, byte tier; skeleton sweep: 1 verse book-wide) -- a proclamation directed outward, role-split from the summons-to-addressee class carried at oshb:Isa.47.8, oshb:Isa.48.1 and oshb:Isa.48.16, so it is not a competing onset here. The row moves from the teaching lament closing the previous row at web:Isa.48.19 into this enacted proclamation. The same opening verse closes on a named referent for the servant word rather than the book's unnamed servant-figure crux: גָּאַ֥ל יְהוָ֖ה עַבְדּ֥וֹ יַעֲקֹֽב (oshb:Isa.48.20, byte tier), “Yahweh has redeemed his servant Jacob!” -- Jacob is the referent stated in the verse's own bytes. The wilderness memory “They didn’t thirst when he led them through the deserts. He caused the waters to flow out of the rock for them. He also split the rock and the waters gushed out.” (web:Isa.48.21) leads into the closing verdict, “There is no peace”, says Yahweh, “for the wicked.”” (web:Isa.48.22), אֵ֣ין שָׁל֔וֹם אָמַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה לָרְשָׁעִֽים (oshb:Isa.48.22, byte tier), the row's own closing verse, ahead of a different frame opening at web:Isa.49.1.
strongest_rejected_alternative: A rival reading holds this departure proclamation inside the same row as the teaching lament of Isa.48.12-Isa.48.19, but the bare imperative lacking a hear-formula is read as a shift strong enough from argued speech to enacted proclamation to open its own row.
literature_type_guess: departure proclamation for the exiles, closing the disputation cycle on a verdict against the wicked

device_notes: The setumah after Isa.48.22 (single-witness, tier-3) falls on this row's own back seam, terminating the row's closing verse. This closing verdict formula, אֵ֣ין שָׁל֔וֹם אָמַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה לָרְשָׁעִֽים (oshb:Isa.48.22, byte tier), recurs later in the book at אֵ֣ין שָׁל֔וֹם אָמַ֥ר אֱלֹהַ֖י לָרְשָׁעִֽים (oshb:Isa.57.21, byte tier) -- byte-identical in every token except the divine-name token itself, so the pair is not a byte-identical refrain and no refrain digit may count both under one object -- the resemblance noted as cross-part texture, not as boundary evidence for either seam. The servant word at Isa.48.20 names Jacob explicitly and is read apart from the book's unnamed servant-figure zones, which this row does not engage.
